payload.goal:
Add exactly 4 independent warehouse analytics modules to the verified W1 codebase.
Create src/analytics/contracts.ts exporting WarehouseProjection with a readonly id and project(scenario), where project returns the answer to that module's question.
Each module answers one question, computed from the W1 Scenario, layout and inventory exports:
- src/analytics/projection-01.ts exports the projection "zone-unit-totals": Total units stored in each zone, keyed by zone id. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-01.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-02.ts exports the projection "sku-unit-totals": Total units of each SKU across the whole warehouse, keyed by SKU id. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-02.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-03.ts exports the projection "bin-occupancy": How many bins hold stock, how many are empty, and how many exist. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-03.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-04.ts exports the projection "sku-bin-spread": Number of distinct bins each SKU occupies, keyed by SKU id. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-04.test.ts.
A module must not import another module; it may import only the fixed contract and W1 exports.
Every answer must be derived from the scenario at run time. Do not hardcode results, and do not duplicate the W1 inventory or layout calculations.
Create src/analytics/registry.ts as the sole consumer of every module, returning all projections in the order the modules are listed above, with its own tests in src/analytics/registry.test.ts.
Preserve all existing W1 behaviour and checks.
Add a package script named study:wide-graph that writes exactly one JSON object to stdout and no other output.
Its JSON must be { "schemaVersion": 1, "moduleCount": 4, "scenario": "thesis-seed-2026", "projections": [ { "projectionId": "<the module's projection id>", "value": <that module's answer> }, … ] } with exactly 4 entries in the order the modules are listed above.
Two invocations from the same commit must emit byte-identical JSON.

root.title: Warehouse analytics projections
root.objective: Add four independent runtime warehouse analytics projections, an ordered registry, and deterministic study JSON output without changing W1 behavior.
expectedOutcomes: Four analytics modules compute their answers from W1 scenario, layout, and inventory exports at run time.
A single registry consumes the modules in the required order.
The study:wide-graph script emits byte-identical JSON for repeated invocations from the same commit.
Existing W1 tests and checks remain valid.

complexitySignals.rationale: The work spans new analytics files plus package script configuration while relying on existing W1 domain and scenario APIs.

cut.rationale: The cut separates the shared contract, each independently testable projection, registry integration, and deterministic script behavior. The four projection leaves are separate because each answers a distinct question and must remain module-isolated; registry and script are integration increments with different consumers and acceptance risks.

complexitySignals.rationale: Small file count but it defines the exported contract that all analytics units consume.

children.title: Zone unit totals projection
children.objective: Implement and test the zone-unit-totals projection from the W1 scenario at run time.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/projection-01.ts exports projection id zone-unit-totals.
The projection returns total units stored in each zone keyed by zone id.
The module imports only the fixed contract and W1 exports.
Focused tests verify runtime derivation from W1 inventory and layout behavior.

complexitySignals.rationale: The slice crosses W1 layout and inventory semantics but has one projection output and one focused test file.

children.title: SKU unit totals projection
children.objective: Implement and test the sku-unit-totals projection from the W1 scenario at run time.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/projection-02.ts exports projection id sku-unit-totals.
The projection returns total units of each SKU across the whole warehouse keyed by SKU id.
The module imports only the fixed contract and W1 exports.
Focused tests verify runtime derivation without hardcoded results or duplicated W1 calculations.

complexitySignals.rationale: This is a narrow inventory aggregation with a stable projection contract and focused assertions.

children.title: Bin occupancy projection
children.objective: Implement and test the bin-occupancy projection from the W1 scenario at run time.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/projection-03.ts exports projection id bin-occupancy.
The projection returns how many bins hold stock, how many are empty, and how many exist.
The module imports only the fixed contract and W1 exports.
Focused tests verify consistency between total bins, stocked bins, and empty bins.

complexitySignals.rationale: This projection must integrate layout existence with inventory stock presence, so validation covers both W1 domains.

children.title: SKU bin spread projection
children.objective: Implement and test the sku-bin-spread projection from the W1 scenario at run time.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/projection-04.ts exports projection id sku-bin-spread.
The projection returns the number of distinct bins each SKU occupies keyed by SKU id.
The module imports only the fixed contract and W1 exports.
Focused tests verify distinct-bin behavior rather than unit totals.

complexitySignals.rationale: The core risk is distinctness semantics over inventory records, with limited repository surface.

children.title: Ordered analytics registry
children.objective: Create the sole consumer registry that returns all four projections in the required order and proves module isolation expectations.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/registry.ts imports every projection module and returns all projections in order: zone-unit-totals, sku-unit-totals, bin-occupancy, sku-bin-spread.
No projection module imports another projection module.
src/analytics/registry.test.ts verifies registry order, module count, and projection ids.

complexitySignals.rationale: The registry is the integration point for all modules and establishes the ordering consumed by the study script.

children.title: Deterministic study output
children.objective: Add the study:wide-graph package script and implementation that emits the exact deterministic JSON object for the thesis seed scenario.
expectedOutcomes: package.json defines study:wide-graph.
The script emits exactly one JSON object to stdout and no other output.
The JSON object has schemaVersion 1, moduleCount 4, scenario thesis-seed-2026, and exactly four projection entries in registry order.
Repeated invocations from the same commit are byte-identical.
Tests cover the emitted JSON shape, ordering, and deterministic serialization.

complexitySignals.rationale: This leaf touches package configuration and validates an observable process-level stdout contract.
